final.investment_thesis:
The bear case wins the entry and loses the enterprise, and the decisive question is whether the entry critique is strong enough to justify doing nothing with 98.5% of this book in non-interest-bearing cash. It is not, but it is strong enough to cap size below the trader's 3%.

What is unrefuted: 9M FY2026 revenue +16.15%, FQ3 revenue +16.36%, FQ3 gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), FQ3 EPS +28.7%, $110.2B of nine-month FCF, $62.2B net cash, current ratio repaired from 0.89x to 1.00x, and a primary trend that never bent — 316.83 sits above a restored stack of 10-EMA 310.41 > 50-SMA 309.44 > VWMA 307.76 > a rising 200-SMA at 281.10, which is 12.7% below spot with no death cross anywhere near it. Every 'crack' the bear lists (inventory +94% with raw materials +260%, ~200bp tax normalization, intangible amortization, buyback deceleration) the bear itself sizes near 1% of annual EPS apiece and explicitly declines to call a business problem. My own record reinforces the asymmetry: the 2026-08-12 AAPL Underweight, which trimmed at 302.25, gave up +5.3% of five-day alpha, and the 07-20 through 07-24 cluster bled 3.2–3.8% each by trimming momentum decay inside a stacked rising structure. The lesson codified then — size by distance-to-invalidation rather than cutting intact trends — applies directly here, where invalidation is 1.48 ATR below spot.

What the bear wins, and where each constructive analyst overreached. The aggressive analyst's expected-value case is invalid on its own inputs: the research plan's 50/30/20 weights are the bull branch conditional on three confirmations that have not occurred (MACD crossover, close above 319.28 on volume, pivot hold), so applying them to a pre-confirmation entry inflates the edge twice over — his base case also claims 'you don't get stopped' inside a 300–323 chop band whose lower half contains the plan's own 307.76 invalidation. His $400 foldable-iPhone note is an unnamed analyst's opinion the world-affairs report flags as non-factual, and he cannot dismiss premium-valuation claims for lacking multiples while sizing off that note. The conservative analyst's rebuttals are the sharpest contributions in the debate: the 07-31 open from 333.43 to 304.81 proves a 305.50 stop is a wish, not an order, in this exact instrument; and one 2.19% session on below-average volume is not a vote on a permanent EU take-rate step-down effective October 1. But his alternative fails on its own arithmetic, and the neutral analyst is right to say so: entering at 319.28 with a 309 stop is 10.28 points of risk against 10.31 to 329.59 — 1.0:1, worse than the 1.13:1 available now, not the 1.6:1 he claims. Waiting has a probability argument, not a payoff argument, and neither can be quantified from this fact set. His 'keeping shares costs nothing' is also false: the existing 4.882 shares carry the identical gap hazard he identifies, so he is declining to size risk, not eliminating it — and under this mandate his confirmation gate is as unexecutable as the stop he criticizes.

The neutral analyst supplies the two corrections I adopt: drop 307.76 as a trim trigger because at 1.18 ATR from spot it is ordinary noise (the aggressive is right about this too), and make the operative risk line a closing basis below the 307.8–309.4 pivot cluster, with 305.50 mental and 300.00 structural — executable in a way an intraday stop is not. Where I differ from the neutral is size: 'mixed setups get half size' is an arbitrary discount, and the account context argues the other way. Total equity is $99,649 with $98,102 in cash earning zero; a 2.5% position gapped to the 300.00 floor loses roughly $120–135, about 0.13% of equity, and the stop-distance loss is under $90. That is not a risk that requires a perfect entry to justify, which is why the answer is a modest add rather than Hold.

What would change it. Escalate toward 3.0% only on a MACD crossover plus a daily close above 319.28 on >55M shares, and cap any pre-commitment at 4.0% — not the aggressive's 5–6% — until a close above the 333–340 July shelf on 55–65M+ volume with MACD above both signal and zero. Reduce back toward 1.5% on a closing basis below the 307.8–309.4 pivot cluster, treating 302.25 and the 300.00 swing floor as the next references and 281.10 as the far structural line; a sub-48% gross-margin FQ4 print with a soft guide or inventory above ~$13–14B converts this to Underweight. No liquidation is warranted by any evidence here — a $62.2B net-cash franchise with 50% gross margins is not a short — and no naked short should be contemplated given demonstrated 4.1x-ATR gap risk.

Stated gaps, which are why the target is 2.5% and not higher: no P/E, EV/EBITDA, consensus estimate or company guidance anywhere in the fact set; no segment or geographic revenue, so 50.06% gross-margin durability versus Services mix is unprovable; no options chain or implied-vol data, so no hedge can be priced; the news sample covers 20 of 143 records with all of August 12–16 blank; and the cause of the 2026-07-31 gap is unresolved, so the 310.69–329.59 band is carried as event risk rather than a target. The EU fee overhaul is a genuine mild negative with precedent risk, but its first clean read is the December quarter, not the next open.
final.time_horizon: 3-6 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print
